etymology: From Hebrew Tsor (צֹר) — "rock," the great Phoenician seaport.
biblical_def: The wealthy Phoenician city north of Israel, ally of David and Solomon, later object of severe prophetic judgment for pride and trade in souls (Ezek 26-28).
webster_summary: Phoenician seaport; trading partner; judged for pride.
webster_full: The famous Phoenician seaport on the Mediterranean coast, ally of Israel under David and Solomon (supplying cedar for the temple), later subject of Ezekiel's most extended prophetic judgment for pride, greed, and trafficking.
scriptures: 1 Kings 5:1
And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants unto Solomon.
Ezekiel 28:2
Because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God.
Matthew 11:21-22
Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works... had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago.
corruption_summary: Treated as a footnote rather than as the case study in commercial pride that Scripture makes it.
corruption_paragraphs: Tyre is the Bible's case study in trade-empire pride. Ezekiel 27-28 still reads as the indictment of every commercial city that loves wealth more than God. The lament over the merchant ships could be sung over modern shipping lanes.
usage: Read Ezekiel 28 to see commercial pride judged.
Tyre and Sidon would have repented; would we?

etymology: From Hebrew Tsidon (צִידוֹן) — "fishing," Phoenicia's older capital.
biblical_def: The ancient Phoenician city north of Tyre; mentioned with Tyre in prophetic judgment; visited by Jesus (Mark 7:24-31).
webster_summary: Ancient Phoenician city, twin of Tyre.
webster_full: The Phoenician city older than Tyre, often coupled with it in Scripture; the home of the Syrophoenician woman whose daughter Jesus delivered, and a stop on Paul's prison journey to Rome.
scriptures: Ezekiel 28:22
Behold, I am against thee, O Zidon; and I will be glorified in the midst of thee.
Mark 7:31
And again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee.
Acts 27:3
And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends.
corruption_summary: Reduced to a place-name; missing the gospel-reach into Gentile territory it represents.
corruption_paragraphs: Jesus' visit to the region of Tyre and Sidon was a deliberate gospel-reach into Gentile soil. The Syrophoenician woman becomes a model of importunate faith. Sidon is not just a port — it is gospel-territory.
usage: The gospel reaches Sidon; the gospel reaches your city.
Hold Sidon and Tyre together in prophetic memory.

etymology: Hebrew Nineweh (נִינְוֵה), capital of Assyria on the Tigris.
biblical_def: The capital of Assyria — the great violent empire — to which Jonah was sent and which repented; later destroyed as Nahum prophesied.
webster_summary: Assyrian capital; Jonah's destination; later destroyed.
webster_full: The mighty capital of the Assyrian empire on the Tigris River; recipient of Jonah's reluctant preaching and astonishing repentance; later destroyed in fulfillment of Nahum's prophecy as the empire fell.
scriptures: Jonah 3:5
So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
Nahum 3:7
Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her?
Matthew 12:41
The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas.
corruption_summary: Read mainly through the children's-story Jonah lens, missing the violent geopolitical context and the prophetic doubleness.
corruption_paragraphs: Nineveh repented under Jonah and was spared a generation; it returned to violence and was destroyed under Nahum. The pattern is grace-then-judgment when grace is rejected. Watch for the pattern in your own city's life.
usage: Pray for Nineveh-cities to repent.
Watch lest Nineveh-grace be wasted.

etymology: Hebrew Edom (אֱדוֹם) — "red," from Esau's red stew or red complexion.
biblical_def: The nation descended from Esau, settled in the rocky region south of the Dead Sea; perpetual antagonist of Israel; subject of the prophet Obadiah's entire book.
webster_summary: Esau's nation, perpetual antagonist of Israel.
webster_full: The nation descended from Esau, brother of Jacob; settled in the rocky highlands south and east of the Dead Sea (Mount Seir); chronically opposed Israel and was condemned by Obadiah and other prophets for hatred of his brother.
scriptures: Genesis 25:30
And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.
Obadiah 1:10
For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.
Numbers 20:18
And Edom said unto him, Thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword.
corruption_summary: Forgotten as a category, missing the long brother-conflict that runs through redemption history.
corruption_paragraphs: Edom is the brother who became the enemy. Esau's bitterness echoes through Obadiah, through Herod (an Edomite who tried to kill the Christ-child), through the persistent biblical theme that hatred of brother is hatred of God's plan.
usage: Edom is the brother-enemy archetype.
Read Obadiah for the indictment.

etymology: Hebrew Moab (מוֹאָב) — descendant of Lot through incest with his daughter.
biblical_def: The nation east of the Dead Sea descended from Lot; chronically idolatrous and at war with Israel; yet from Moab came Ruth, ancestress of David and Christ.
webster_summary: Lot's nation east of the Dead Sea; home of Ruth.
webster_full: The nation east of the Dead Sea descended from Lot's older daughter; chronic enemy of Israel and worshippers of Chemosh; yet through Ruth the Moabitess God brought the line of David and Jesus.
scriptures: Genesis 19:37
And the firstborn bare a son, and called his name Moab: the same is the father of the Moabites.
Ruth 1:16
Whither thou goest, I will go... thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.
Numbers 25:1
And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.
corruption_summary: Reduced to enemy-stereotype, missing the redeeming Ruth-thread that pulls Moab into the messianic line.
corruption_paragraphs: Moab is enemy and ancestress at once. Sin in the cave; salvation through Ruth. The same nation that seduced Israel at Baal-Peor produced the great-grandmother of David. Grace breaks the bloodline rules.
usage: Moab and grace meet in Ruth.
Bloodlines do not bind God's mercy.

etymology: Hebrew Gilead (גִּלְעָד) — "heap of testimony," from Jacob and Laban's covenant pile.
biblical_def: The mountainous region east of the Jordan, fertile and famous for its balm; allotted to Reuben, Gad, and half-Manasseh; home of Elijah, Jephthah, and Jair.
webster_summary: Mountainous trans-Jordan region; balm-producing.
webster_full: The fertile mountainous region east of the Jordan River; allotted to the eastern tribes; renowned for its balm of healing; home of judges (Jephthah, Jair) and the prophet Elijah the Tishbite.
scriptures: Jeremiah 8:22
Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there? why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?
1 Kings 17:1
And Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab...
Genesis 31:48
And Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and thee this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed.
corruption_summary: Reduced to a metaphor in spirituals ("there is a balm in Gilead") without anchoring in its biblical geography and people.
corruption_paragraphs: Gilead is real soil — the eastern mountain country where Elijah was raised, where balm flowed, where covenant was sworn. The spiritual leans on the geography. Recover the place; you recover the song.
usage: The balm of Gilead is the healing the gospel brings.
Elijah the Tishbite — a Gileadite shaped by Gilead's wilderness.

etymology: Hebrew Bashan (בָּשָׁן) — fertile region east of the Sea of Galilee.
biblical_def: The fertile, well-watered region east of the Sea of Galilee, famous for its strong cattle and oaks; defeated under Og the giant and given to half-Manasseh (Num 21; Deut 3).
webster_summary: Fertile region east of Galilee; Og's kingdom.
webster_full: The lush, well-watered region north and east of the Sea of Galilee; conquered from Og, last of the Rephaim giants; famed for strong cattle and tall oaks; symbol of fat prosperity in the prophets.
scriptures: Numbers 21:33
And they turned and went up by the way of Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan went out against them.
Psalm 22:12
Many bulls have compassed me: strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round.
Amos 4:1
Hear this word, ye kine of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria.
corruption_summary: Reduced to obscure place-name, missing the symbolic weight Scripture gives it for prosperous strength.
corruption_paragraphs: Bashan is more than geography in Scripture. Its bulls and oaks become symbols of brute strength and fat luxury. Psalm 22's 'bulls of Bashan' surrounding the Sufferer at the cross is a deliberate echo. Read Bashan symbolically.
usage: Bulls of Bashan oppose the cross.
Bashan represents fat strength under judgment.

etymology: Hebrew Charan (חָרָן) — caravan crossroads in upper Mesopotamia.
biblical_def: The city in upper Mesopotamia where Terah died, where Abram waited before Canaan, and where Jacob fled to Laban; a transitional city in patriarchal pilgrimage.
webster_summary: Mesopotamian crossroads; Abram's pause; Jacob's exile.
webster_full: The city in upper Mesopotamia (modern southeast Turkey) where Terah died, where Abraham paused on the journey from Ur to Canaan, and where Jacob spent his twenty years of exile with Laban.
scriptures: Genesis 11:31
And Terah took Abram his son... to go into the land of Canaan; and they came unto Haran, and dwelt there.
Genesis 12:4
So Abram departed... and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.
Genesis 28:10
And Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.
corruption_summary: Treated as travel-trivia, missing how often Haran is the in-between place where God shapes pilgrims.
corruption_paragraphs: Haran is the in-between. Abraham's faith is tested in Haran's delay; Jacob's character is forged in Haran's exile. God's people are often shaped not at the destination but in the long Haran-pause.
usage: Trust God in your Haran-season.
Faith is tested in delays.

etymology: Hebrew Ur Kasdim (אוּר כַּשְׂדִּים) — Ur of the Chaldeans, in southern Mesopotamia.
biblical_def: The ancient city in southern Mesopotamia from which God called Abram out by faith into Canaan (Gen 11:31; 15:7; Acts 7:2-4).
webster_summary: Abram's home city in southern Mesopotamia.
webster_full: The ancient Sumerian city in southern Mesopotamia (modern southern Iraq) from which Terah and Abram migrated; the starting point of the Abrahamic call to leave kindred and country and follow God to a land yet unseen.
scriptures: Genesis 11:31
And Terah took Abram his son... and they went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldees.
Genesis 15:7
I am the LORD that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land to inherit it.
Acts 7:2-3
The God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia... Get thee out of thy country.
corruption_summary: Forgotten as the starting point, so the Abrahamic faith-leap loses its concreteness.
corruption_paragraphs: Ur was an advanced city; leaving it for tents in Canaan was downward mobility, not upward. Faith is often an exit from sophistication into pilgrimage. The God of glory called Abraham out of Ur; He calls us out of our cities too.
usage: Faith leaves Ur for Canaan.
Recover the cost of Abraham's call.

etymology: Hebrew Midyan (מִדְיָן) — descendants of Abraham through Keturah, occupying the desert east of the Gulf of Aqaba.
biblical_def: The desert region east of the Gulf of Aqaba where Moses fled and married Zipporah, and from which Gideon would later deliver Israel.
webster_summary: Desert east of Aqaba; Moses' refuge; Gideon's enemy.
webster_full: The desert region southeast of Canaan, descended from Abraham and Keturah; the place of Moses' 40-year shepherding refuge and his marriage to Zipporah; later the oppressor against whom Gideon was raised up.
scriptures: Exodus 2:15
Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.
Exodus 3:1
Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Midian.
Judges 6:1
And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD: and the LORD delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years.
corruption_summary: Confused with the people-group elsewhere; under-read for its shaping role in Moses' formation.
corruption_paragraphs: Midian is where Moses learned to shepherd before God called him to shepherd Israel. The 40 wilderness years there were not wasted years — they were the seminary God ran for the deliverer. Trust your Midian.
usage: Midian shaped Moses; trust the desert season.
Gideon delivered Israel from Midian's tyranny.

etymology: Hebrew Pelesheth (פְּלֶשֶׁת) — "land of immigrants," the coastal pentapolis.
biblical_def: The coastal region of Canaan inhabited by the Philistines (a Sea People), comprising five great cities: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron, and Gath; perpetual enemy of Israel until David's reign.
webster_summary: Coastal pentapolis; Israel's perpetual enemy.
webster_full: The coastal plain of southern Canaan inhabited by the Philistines, a Sea-Peoples migration; comprising the five-city league of Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron, and Gath; chief enemy of Israel through the period of the judges and early kings.
scriptures: Joshua 13:3
From Sihor, which is before Egypt... five lords of the Philistines; the Gazathites, and the Ashdothites, the Eshkalonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites.
Judges 13:1
And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
1 Samuel 17:50
So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone.
corruption_summary: Used as a political insult today, severed from the actual Bronze-Age Sea-People migration that produced them.
corruption_paragraphs: The Philistines were not Arabs — they were Aegean migrants, technologically advanced in iron, and the chief military threat of pre-monarchic Israel. The modern political appropriation of the name does not match the biblical or archaeological people.
usage: Philistia is the Bronze-Age Sea-People region.
Read the pentapolis behind the headlines.

etymology: Hebrew Gat (גַּת) — "winepress," Philistine city of giants.
biblical_def: One of the five Philistine pentapolis cities; home of Goliath and the giants; David's place of refuge from Saul (1 Sam 21).
webster_summary: Philistine city; Goliath's home; David's refuge.
webster_full: One of the five great Philistine cities; home of Goliath and his giant brothers; ironically the place where David fled twice when running from Saul, feigning madness before Achish king of Gath.
scriptures: 1 Samuel 17:4
And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath.
1 Samuel 21:10
And David arose, and fled that day for fear of Saul, and went to Achish the king of Gath.
2 Samuel 1:20
Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon.
corruption_summary: Read as a footnote rather than as the dramatic stage on which David's story repeatedly turned.
corruption_paragraphs: Gath keeps showing up: the giant-city, the refuge-city, the embarrassment-city ('tell it not in Gath'). David's life loops through Gath. The geography repeats; God draws lessons in repetition.
usage: Gath is where giants and refugees both lived.
Tell it not in Gath.

etymology: Hebrew Ashdod (אַשְׁדּוֹד) — "powerful," northern Philistine pentapolis city.
biblical_def: Philistine city where the captured ark of God toppled Dagon and afflicted the city with tumors before being sent on (1 Sam 5).
webster_summary: Philistine city where Dagon fell before the ark.
webster_full: One of the five Philistine cities; site where the captured ark of YHWH was placed in Dagon's temple, and Dagon was repeatedly toppled before being broken; tumors broke out and the ark was sent on.
scriptures: 1 Samuel 5:1-3
And the Philistines took the ark of God... and brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it by Dagon. And when they of Ashdod arose early on the morrow, behold, Dagon was fallen upon his face.
1 Samuel 5:6
But the hand of the LORD was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with emerods.
Nehemiah 13:23-24
In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod... and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod.
corruption_summary: Forgotten as obscure; missing the great Dagon-falls-before-ark theology of the chapter.
corruption_paragraphs: Ashdod is where the rival god falls. The Philistines thought they had captured YHWH; they had brought a sleeping lion into the temple. Every false god collapses where the true God is set down.
usage: Where YHWH is set down, Dagon falls.
Read 1 Samuel 5 to recover the joy.

etymology: Hebrew Ashkelon (אַשְׁקְלוֹן) — Philistine coastal city.
biblical_def: One of the five Philistine cities; subject of repeated prophetic judgment (Jer 47; Zeph 2; Zech 9); David's lament names it alongside Gath.
webster_summary: Philistine coastal city under prophetic judgment.
webster_full: One of the five great Philistine cities, on the Mediterranean coast; sacked and prophesied against repeatedly by Jeremiah, Zephaniah, and Zechariah; mentioned in David's lament for Saul and Jonathan.
scriptures: Judges 14:19
And the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon, and slew thirty men of them.
Jeremiah 47:5
Baldness is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is cut off.
2 Samuel 1:20
Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon.
corruption_summary: Reduced to one of the lesser pentapolis cities, missing how often the prophets target it.
corruption_paragraphs: Ashkelon recurs in the prophets. It is one of the five test-cases of God's judgment on Philistia. Read Jeremiah 47, Zephaniah 2, and Zechariah 9 together — Ashkelon is a refrain.
usage: Read the prophets' Ashkelon-oracles together.
Cities under judgment recur in Scripture's grammar.

etymology: Hebrew Eqron (עֶקְרוֹן) — northernmost of the Philistine pentapolis.
biblical_def: The northernmost Philistine city; site of Baal-zebub the false god whom Ahaziah consulted (2 Kings 1:2-4); recipient of prophetic judgment.
webster_summary: Philistine city of Baal-zebub.
webster_full: The northernmost of the five Philistine cities; home of the false god Baal-zebub (lord of flies) whom King Ahaziah of Israel sent to consult instead of YHWH, drawing Elijah's rebuke and Ahaziah's death.
scriptures: 1 Samuel 5:10
Therefore they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And it came to pass, as the ark of God came to Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out.
2 Kings 1:2
Ahaziah... sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.
Amos 1:8
And I will turn mine hand against Ekron: and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish.
corruption_summary: Forgotten — but its idol Baal-zebub becomes the New Testament's Beelzebub, prince of demons.
corruption_paragraphs: Baal-zebub of Ekron — Lord of Flies — became Beelzebub in the New Testament, ruler of the demonic realm. The Bible-historic name traveled. Read Ekron and Beelzebub together; the demonization of false gods continues.
usage: Ekron's idol haunts the New Testament.
Beelzebub is Baal-zebub of Ekron.

etymology: Hebrew Azzah (עַזָּה) — "strong," southernmost Philistine city.
biblical_def: Southernmost of the Philistine pentapolis; the city whose gates Samson tore off and where he was finally bound, blinded, and killed in the temple of Dagon (Judg 16).
webster_summary: Philistine city of Samson's gate-tearing and death.
webster_full: The southernmost Philistine city, on the road between Egypt and the East; site of Samson's gate-tearing exploit and his final bringing-down of Dagon's temple in his death.
scriptures: Judges 16:3
And Samson lay till midnight, and arose at midnight, and took the doors of the gate of the city, and the two posts, and went away with them, bar and all.
Judges 16:21
But the Philistines took him, and put out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass.
Acts 8:26
And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza.
corruption_summary: Treated only as a modern political flashpoint; missing the deep biblical place it has been since Samson.
corruption_paragraphs: Gaza is also the road on which Philip met the Ethiopian eunuch and baptized him. The same place that bound Samson was the place where the gospel went to Africa. Geography repeats; redemption advances.
usage: Gaza is Samson's death and Philip's road.
The gospel runs the road that bound the strongman.

etymology: Hebrew Yapho (יָפוֹ) — "beautiful," the ancient Mediterranean port (modern Jaffa).
biblical_def: The Mediterranean port of Israel; from which Jonah fled to Tarshish; where Peter raised Tabitha and received the rooftop vision opening the gospel to Gentiles (Acts 9-10).
webster_summary: Israel's port; Jonah's flight; Peter's rooftop vision.
webster_full: The Mediterranean port of ancient Israel (modern Jaffa); from which Jonah took ship to flee; where Peter raised Tabitha and on the rooftop received the vision of the great sheet that opened the gospel to Cornelius and the Gentiles.
scriptures: Jonah 1:3
But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD, and went down to Joppa.
Acts 9:36
Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha... full of good works.
Acts 10:9
Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour.
corruption_summary: Forgotten as the pivot point where the New Testament gospel breaks Gentile-ward.
corruption_paragraphs: Joppa is the Bible's threshold between covenants. From Joppa Jonah fled rather than preach to Gentiles; in Joppa Peter received the vision that sent him to Cornelius. The same port; the great reversal.
usage: From Joppa the gospel turned to Gentiles.
Two fugitives at the same port; one obeyed.

etymology: Hebrew Megiddo (מְגִדּוֹ) — fortress on the Jezreel plain.
biblical_def: The strategic fortress overlooking the Jezreel valley; site of many Old Testament battles and source of the term 'Armageddon' (Har-Megiddo, Mount of Megiddo) — the apocalyptic battlefield (Rev 16:16).
webster_summary: Strategic fortress; root of Armageddon.
webster_full: The strategic fortress city dominating the Jezreel valley, the chokepoint of trade routes between Egypt and Mesopotamia; site of repeated Old Testament battles; the geographical source of the apocalyptic term Armageddon (Har-Megiddo).
scriptures: Judges 5:19
The kings came and fought, then fought the kings of Canaan in Taanach by the waters of Megiddo.
Pharaohnechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria... and king Josiah went against him; and he slew him at Megiddo.
Revelation 16:16
And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon.
corruption_summary: Detached from real geography in apocalyptic speculation, leaving Armageddon as cosmic abstraction rather than the very real Jezreel battlefield.
corruption_paragraphs: Armageddon is Hebrew Har Megiddo — the mountain of Megiddo. Real soil. The very plain where Deborah and Barak fought Sisera and where Josiah died at Necho's hand. The end-time battle is named for a real, repeated battlefield.
usage: Megiddo is the world's perpetual battlefield.
Armageddon is named for a real plain.

etymology: Modern English; biblical Hebrew yam ha-melach (Salt Sea) or yam ha-aravah (Sea of the Plain).
biblical_def: The salt lake at the lowest point on earth, in the Jordan Rift Valley; biblical 'Salt Sea' bordering Israel, Moab, and Edom; site of Sodom and Gomorrah's destruction; healing-water in Ezekiel's eschatological vision.
webster_summary: Salt lake at earth's lowest point.
webster_full: The salt-saturated lake at the lowest land elevation on earth, fed by the Jordan; biblical 'Salt Sea' or 'Sea of the Plain'; bordering Judea, Moab, and Edom; site of Sodom and Gomorrah's overthrow; in Ezekiel 47 the river from the temple makes its waters fresh and teeming with fish.
scriptures: Genesis 14:3
All these were joined together in the vale of Siddim, which is the salt sea.
Numbers 34:12
The border shall... go down to Jordan, and the goings out of it shall be at the salt sea.
Ezekiel 47:8-9
These waters issue out... into the sea: which being brought forth into the sea, the waters shall be healed.
corruption_summary: Reduced to a tourist curiosity, missing both the destruction it remembers and the healing Ezekiel promises.
corruption_paragraphs: The Dead Sea is monument and prophecy. The destruction of Sodom is buried beneath it; Ezekiel sees the river from the temple healing it. End-time renewal will reach even what is most dead. Read both layers.
usage: The Dead Sea remembers Sodom.
Ezekiel's river will heal even the Dead Sea.

etymology: Greek Tarsos (Ταρσός) — capital of Cilicia in southeast Asia Minor.
biblical_def: The free Roman city in Cilicia; birthplace and citizenship-city of Paul the apostle (Acts 9:11; 21:39; 22:3).
webster_summary: Paul's birth city; Roman free city in Cilicia.
webster_full: The Roman free city in Cilicia (southeast Asia Minor), capital of the province; renowned for its university and Stoic philosophy; the birthplace of Saul (Paul) of Tarsus, who was a Roman citizen by birth there.
scriptures: Acts 9:11
Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus.
Acts 21:39
I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city.
Acts 22:3
I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel.
corruption_summary: Treated as biographical trivia, missing how Tarsus shaped Paul's mind and gospel-reach.
corruption_paragraphs: Tarsus shaped Paul. Greco-Roman education, philosophical engagement, citizenship privilege — all came from Tarsus. The man God used to bring the gospel to the Greco-Roman world was made for that world by his Tarsus upbringing.
usage: Tarsus made Paul; Damascus remade him.
God prepares ministers in their cities.

etymology: Greek Korinthos (Κόρινθος) — strategic Greek port-city on the isthmus.
biblical_def: The cosmopolitan Greek port-city on the isthmus connecting the Peloponnese to mainland Greece; legendary for sexual immorality; site of Paul's 18-month church-plant and recipient of two New Testament letters.
webster_summary: Cosmopolitan Greek port; Paul's troubled church.
webster_full: The wealthy, cosmopolitan port-city of Greece on the isthmus joining the Peloponnese to the mainland; notorious for sexual license (the verb 'to corinthianize' meant to fornicate); site of Paul's eighteen-month church-plant and recipient of two surviving canonical letters.
scriptures: Acts 18:1
After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth.
Acts 18:11
And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
1 Corinthians 6:11
And such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified.
corruption_summary: Read as merely backdrop to Paul's letters, missing the city's deep moral collapse that made the gospel scandalous and beautiful there.
corruption_paragraphs: Corinth was the Vegas of antiquity. Paul founded a church among prostitutes, sexually broken men, and the religiously confused — and the gospel held. 1 Corinthians 6:11 — 'and such were some of you' — is one of the great gospel-power statements.
usage: The gospel works in Corinths.
Read 1 Corinthians 6:11 with awe.

etymology: Greek Ephesos (Ἔφεσος) — the great commercial city of Asia Minor.
biblical_def: The leading commercial-religious city of Roman Asia, home of the temple of Artemis (Diana); site of Paul's three-year ministry; recipient of the Ephesian letter and one of the seven letters of Revelation.
webster_summary: Asia's leading city; Paul's three-year base.
webster_full: The leading commercial and religious city of Roman Asia Minor; home of the great temple of Artemis (Diana), one of the seven wonders; site of Paul's three-year ministry and the eventual home of the apostle John; recipient of the Ephesian epistle and the first of the seven letters of Revelation.
scriptures: Acts 19:10
And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus.
Ephesians 1:3
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ.
Revelation 2:4
Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love.
corruption_summary: Read as a backdrop rather than as the case study in long-haul gospel impact (a city's idol-economy shaken).
corruption_paragraphs: Acts 19 is a study in how the gospel can shake a city's economy. The silversmiths of Artemis lost business as Christians stopped buying idols. Three years of teaching reshaped a region. Be patient with three-year ministries.
usage: Three years in Ephesus reshaped a region.
First-love must not be left.

etymology: Hebrew Lemekh (לֶמֶךְ) — two figures: Cain's polygamous descendant, and Methuselah's son (Noah's father).
biblical_def: Two Old Testament figures: (1) the Cainite Lamech who introduced polygamy and boasted in vengeance (Gen 4:19-24), and (2) the Sethite Lamech who fathered Noah (Gen 5:28-29).
webster_summary: Two pre-flood figures of contrasting lines.
webster_full: Two distinct pre-flood figures: the Cainite Lamech, polygamist and proud avenger ('I have slain a man for wounding me'); and the Sethite Lamech, son of Methuselah and father of Noah, who named his son hoping for relief from the cursed ground.
scriptures: Genesis 4:19
And Lamech took unto him two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
Genesis 4:23-24
If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.
Genesis 5:28-29
Lamech... begat a son: and he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands.
corruption_summary: Confused as one figure rather than read as the deliberate genealogical contrast Genesis sets up.
corruption_paragraphs: Genesis lays the two Lamechs in deliberate parallel. Cain's line ends in vengeful Lamech; Seth's line ends in hopeful Lamech who fathers Noah. The genealogies are sermons; read them as such.
usage: Two Lamechs; two lines; two destinies.
Genealogies preach.

etymology: Hebrew Sheth (שֵׁת) — "appointed," the third son of Adam born after Abel's murder.
biblical_def: The third son of Adam and Eve, given as the replacement for Abel; head of the godly line through whom the messianic seed advanced (Gen 4:25-26).
webster_summary: Adam's third son; replacement for Abel; godly line.
webster_full: The third son of Adam and Eve, given as God's appointment after Cain murdered Abel; head of the line through which the godly seed advanced — Enosh, Methuselah, Noah, and ultimately the Messiah.
scriptures: Genesis 4:25
And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.
Genesis 4:26
Then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.
Luke 3:38
Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.
corruption_summary: Forgotten in favor of Cain and Abel; missing how Seth is God's deliberate continuation of the messianic seed.
corruption_paragraphs: Cain killed Abel and the line of promise looked dead. Then God appointed Seth — and the messianic line continued through him. The pattern repeats: human violence does not undo divine purpose; God appoints a Seth where an Abel has fallen.
usage: God appoints His Seth where the world kills its Abel.
Read Seth's line as the messianic thread.

etymology: Hebrew Tubal-Qayin (תּוּבַל קַיִן) — son of Lamech the Cainite, the first metalworker.
biblical_def: The pre-flood Cainite remembered as the first artificer of bronze and iron tools (Gen 4:22) — civilization's first metallurgist.
webster_summary: First metalworker; pre-flood Cainite.
webster_full: The Cainite descendant of Lamech remembered in Genesis 4 as the first to forge bronze and iron tools; one of three brothers who pioneered, respectively, livestock, music, and metallurgy.
scriptures: Genesis 4:22
And Zillah, she also bare Tubalcain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron.
Genesis 4:20-21
Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents... his brother's name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.
Genesis 4:24
If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.
corruption_summary: Forgotten or treated as oddity; missing how Genesis 4 explains civilization's origins through the Cainite line.
corruption_paragraphs: Genesis 4 traces civilization's origins — pastoral, musical, metallurgical — through Cain's line. The text is not anti-civilization; it is showing that culture flourishes even outside the covenant. Common grace falls on Tubal-Cain.
usage: Civilization came through Cain's line.
Common grace gives gifts to all.
